fields_before.title: Pandora's Box Was Never a Box | What the Ancient Sources Say
fields_before.description:
Pandora's famous box began as a great storage jar. Follow the container from Hesiod's poems to a later Greek fable, Erasmus's book of proverbs printed in 1508, and the paintings that gave Pandora her box.

This video uses synthetic narration and clearly labelled AI-generated reconstructions. Reconstructions are illustrative; they are not historical evidence or exact reconstructions of real places. Modern interpretations are kept separate from ancient accounts.

Chapters
00:00 The Box Everyone Knows
00:51 Made by the Gods
02:07 A Jar, Not a Box
03:39 Other Ancient Versions
04:28 How the Jar Became a Box
05:58 Jar, Box, and Story

Sources

- Hesiod, Theogony 570–612, tr. H. G. Evelyn-White (1914) — https://www.theoi.com/Text/HesiodTheogony.html
- Pausanias, Description of Greece 1.24.7, tr. W. H. S. Jones (1918) — https://www.theoi.com/Text/Pausanias1B.html
- Babrius, Fables 58, tr. James Davies (1860) — https://elfinspell.com/ClassicalTexts/Babrius/Part1-Fables40-79.html
- Erasmus, Adagiorum chiliades, I.i.31, Venice: Aldus, 1508, fol. 12r (ULiège Library) — https://donum.uliege.be/handle/2268.1/10063
- Apuleius, Metamorphoses 6.16–21, tr. William Adlington (1566) — https://www.gutenberg.org/files/1666/1666-h/1666-h.htm
Further reading: Dora and Erwin Panofsky, Pandora's Box: The Changing Aspects of a Mythical Symbol (1956).
